unit.title: JavaScript: functions
unit.description: Writing a function, calling it, parameters and arguments, return

cards.definition: Creates a reusable block of code with the keyword function, a name, parentheses and braces.
Runs a function: its name followed by parentheses. Without the parentheses, nothing runs.
cards.example: greet(); runs the code inside greet.

cards.definition: A name between the parentheses of a function that receives a value each time the function is called.
cards.example: In function double(n), n is filled in at each call.

cards.definition: The actual value you pass to a function when you call it, between the parentheses.
Sends a value back to the code that called the function, and stops the function at that point.
cards.example: function double(n) { return n * 2; } then double(4) gives 8.

cards.definition: The habit of putting repeated code in one function and calling it, instead of copying it around.
cards.example: One formatPrice() used on every page instead of five copies.

choices: A named block of code you can run again and again
A list of values between square brackets
A value that is either true or false
A note that the computer ignores
exercises.explain: A function packs instructions under a name. You write them once and run them as often as you need.
whyWrong: A list of values between brackets is an array.
A true or false value is a boolean.
A note ignored by the computer is a comment.

choices: Hi! twice
Hi! once
Nothing
greet twice
exercises.explain: Writing a function does not run it. Each call, greet(), runs its code once.
whyWrong: The function is called two times, so it runs two times.
A function runs only when called, and here it is called twice.
The function prints its text, not its name.

choices: Nothing, because it is never called
Hello, because it runs by itself
hello, the name of the function
An error, as nothing is called
exercises.explain: Writing a function only defines it. To run it, call it with its name and parentheses: hello();
whyWrong: A function never runs by itself: it must be called.
Even when called, it would print its text, not its name.
Defining a function without calling it is allowed.

choices: double
exercises.explain: The argument 4 goes into the parameter n. return sends back 4 * 2, and console.log prints it.
whyWrong: 4 is the value passed in; the function sends it back doubled.
The expression is computed with n equal to 4.
console.log prints the value sent back, not the name.

exercises.prompt: In function greet(name), what is name?
choices: A parameter: it receives a value at each call
The value sent back by the function
The text shown on the screen
A reserved word of JavaScript
exercises.explain: Parameters are listed between the parentheses. greet("Ana") fills name with "Ana".
whyWrong: The value sent back comes from return.
name holds whatever is passed in; it is not shown by itself.
name is an ordinary name chosen by the developer.

choices: Hi Mia
Hi name
greet("Mia")
Mia
exercises.explain: "Mia" is the argument: it fills the parameter name, and return sends back "Hi Mia".
whyWrong: name is replaced by the value passed in, "Mia".
The call runs the function; its code is not printed.
The function adds "Hi " in front of the name.

exercises.prompt: Code written after return, inside the same function, still runs.
exercises.explain: return sends the value back and ends the function at once. The lines below it never run.

exercises.prompt: Build the line that calls the function add with the numbers 2 and 3.
exercises.explain: Call a function with its name, then the arguments in parentheses, separated by commas: add(2, 3).

exercises.prompt: The console shows undefined instead of 10. Which line is wrong?
exercises.explain: The sum is computed but never sent back. Without return, a function gives undefined. Write return a + b;

exercises.prompt: Why put code in a function instead of copying it in three places?
choices: To fix it once and reuse it everywhere
To make the images of the page load faster
To hide the code from the visitors
Because copying lines is forbidden
exercises.explain: Do not repeat yourself: one function, many calls. A fix inside the function fixes every place that uses it.
whyWrong: Functions organize code; they do not speed up images.
Code inside a function is just as visible.
Copying is allowed, just much harder to maintain.
